sanskrit: prāṇināṃ sarvato vāyuś ceṣṭā vartayate pṛthak prāṇanāc caiva bhūtānāṃ prāṇa ity abhidhīyate
english: In all living beings the wind sustains, severally, the diverse motions of life; and because it makes creatures breathe, it is called prāṇa, the breath of life.

sanskrit: prerayaty abhrasaṃghātān dhūmajāṃś coṣmajāṃś ca yaḥ prathamaḥ prathame mārge pravaho nāma so 'nilaḥ
english: That wind which drives onward the massed banks of cloud, those born of smoke and those born of heat, is the first, moving upon the first path; it is the wind named Pravaha.

sanskrit: ambare sneham abhrebhyas taḍidbhyaś cottamadyutiḥ āvaho nāma saṃvāti dvitīyaḥ śvasano nadan
english: That of surpassing splendour which gathers the moisture in the sky from the clouds and from the lightnings is the second; named Āvaha, it blows roaring as it breathes.

sanskrit: udayaṃ jyotiṣāṃ śaśvat somādīnāṃ karoti yaḥ antardeheṣu codānaṃ yaṃ vadanti maharṣayaḥ
english: That which ceaselessly brings about the rising of the luminaries, of the moon and the rest, and which within the bodies of beings the great seers call by the name of udāna,

sanskrit: yaś caturbhyaḥ samudrebhyo vāyur dhārayate jalam uddhṛtyādadate cāpo jīmūtebhyo 'mbare 'nilaḥ
english: that wind which holds up the waters drawn from the four oceans, and which, lifting them, draws the waters from the rain-clouds into the sky,

sanskrit: yo 'dbhiḥ saṃyojya jīmūtān parjanyāya prayacchati udvaho nāma varṣiṣṭhas tritīyaḥ sa sadāgatiḥ
english: that which, charging the rain-clouds with water, delivers them to Parjanya, the rain-god — most abundant in showers, the third, ever in motion, is named Udvaha.

sanskrit: samuhyamānā bahudhā yena nīlāḥ pṛthag ghanāḥ varṣamokṣakṛtārambhās te bhavanti ghanāghanāḥ
english: By it the dark clouds, borne along in many directions and gathered apart, set themselves to release their rain and become massed thunderheads piled cloud on cloud.

sanskrit: saṃhatā yena cāviddhā bhavanti nadatāṃ nadāḥ rakṣaṇārthāya saṃbhūtā meghatvam upayānti ca
english: Welded together and pierced through by it, the clouds become the rivers of the thundering sky; gathered for the protection of the world, they take on the form of clouds.

sanskrit: yo 'sau vahati devānāṃ vimānāni vihāyasā caturthaḥ saṃvaho nāma vāyuḥ sa girimardanaḥ
english: That which bears the celestial cars of the gods through the firmament is the fourth, the wind named Saṃvaha, the crusher of mountains.

sanskrit: yena vegavatā rugṇā rūkṣeṇārujatā rasān vāyunā vihatā meghā na bhavanti balāhakāḥ
english: That swift and parching wind which shatters the clouds and dries up their savour — struck by it, the clouds break apart and form no thunderheads.

sanskrit: dāruṇotpātasaṃcāro nabhasaḥ stanayitnumān pañcamaḥ sa mahāvego vivaho nāma mārutaḥ
english: Coursing on with dreadful portents, carrying the thunder of the heavens, of mighty speed, is the fifth wind, named Vivaha.

sanskrit: yasmin pāriplave divyā vahanty āpo vihāyasā puṇyaṃ cākāśagaṅgāyās toyaṃ viṣṭabhya tiṣṭhati
english: Upon it, as upon a floating raft, the celestial waters are borne through the sky, and the holy water of the heavenly Gaṅgā is held up and abides.

sanskrit: dūrāt pratihato yasminn ekaraśmir divākaraḥ yonir aṃśusahasrasya yena bhāti vasuṃdharā
english: Within it the maker of day, the sun, whose single ray is turned back from afar, becomes the source of a thousand beams by which the earth is made to shine.

sanskrit: yasmād āpyāyate somo nidhir divyo 'mṛtasya ca ṣaṣṭhaḥ parivaho nāma sa vāyur javatāṃ varaḥ
english: By it the moon, that celestial treasury of nectar, is replenished; the sixth, named Parivaha, is that wind, foremost among the swift.

sanskrit: sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ prāṇān yo 'ntakāle nirasyati yasya vartmānuvartete mṛtyuvaivasvatāv ubhau
english: That which at the hour of the end casts forth the life-breaths of all that breathe, in whose track both Death and the son of Vivasvat — Yama — follow after,

sanskrit: samyag anvīkṣatāṃ buddhyā śāntayādhyātmanityayā dhyānābhyāsābhirāmāṇāṃ yo 'mṛtatvāya kalpate
english: that which, for those who look rightly with the understanding by an ever-spiritual peace and who delight in the practice of meditation, conduces to immortality —

sanskrit: yaṃ samāsādya vegena diśām antaṃ prapedire dakṣasya daśa putrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi prajāpateḥ
english: reaching which with its swiftness, the ten thousand sons of Dakṣa, the lord of creatures, attained to the ends of the quarters,

sanskrit: yena sṛṣṭaḥ parābhūto yāty eva na nivartate parāvaho nāma paro vāyuḥ sa duratikramaḥ
english: that which, once it has cast a thing forth, vanquished, it goes on and never returns — that highest wind, hard to withstand, is named Parāvaha.

sanskrit: evam ete 'diteḥ putrā mārutāḥ paramādbhutāḥ anāramantaḥ saṃvānti sarvagāḥ sarvadhāriṇaḥ
english: Thus these sons of Aditi, the most wondrous Maruts, never resting, blow on every side, pervading all, upholding all.

sanskrit: etat tu mahad āścaryaṃ yad ayaṃ parvatottamaḥ kampitaḥ sahasā tena vāyunābhipravāyatā
english: And here is the great marvel: that this noblest of mountains was suddenly set trembling by that wind as it blew full against it.

sanskrit: viṣṇor niḥśvāsavāto 'yaṃ yadā vegasamīritaḥ sahasodīryate tāta jagat pravyathate tadā
english: This wind is the breath of Viṣṇu, my son; when, driven by its own force, it is suddenly stirred up, the whole world quakes in distress.

sanskrit: tasmād brahmavido brahma nādhīyante 'tivāyati vāyor vāyubhayaṃ hy uktaṃ brahma tat pīḍitaṃ bhavet
english: Therefore the knowers of the Veda do not recite the sacred word while the wind blows too strongly; for fear of the wind is enjoined, and that recitation would be marred.

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ parāśarasutaḥ prabhuḥ uktvā putram adhīṣveti vyomagaṅgām ayāt tadā
english: Having spoken these words, the lord, the son of Parāśara, and having bidden his son, "Resume thy study," then betook himself to the heavenly Gaṅgā of the sky.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etasminn antare śūnye nāradaḥ samupāgamat śukaṃ svādhyāyanirataṃ vedārthān vaktum īpsitān
english: Bhīṣma said: In this interval, when the place was empty, Nārada drew near to Śuka, who was absorbed in his recitation, intending to expound the meanings of the Vedas that he longed to hear.

sanskrit: devarṣiṃ tu śuko dṛṣṭvā nāradaṃ samupasthitam arghyapūrveṇa vidhinā vedoktenābhyapūjayat
english: Beholding the divine sage Nārada come before him, Śuka honoured him with the rite ordained in the Veda, offering first the welcome-water.

sanskrit: nārado 'thābravīt prīto brūhi brahmavidāṃ vara kena tvāṃ śreyasā tāta yojayāmīti hṛṣṭavat
english: Then Nārada said, well pleased and joyful, "Speak, O best of those who know the Absolute; with what blessing, my son, shall I unite thee?"

sanskrit: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā śukaḥ provāca bhārata asmiṃl loke hitaṃ yat syāt tena māṃ yoktum arhasi
english: Hearing Nārada's words, Śuka replied, O descendant of Bharata: "With that which would be of benefit in this world it is fitting that thou shouldst unite me."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tattvaṃ jijñāsatāṃ pūrvam ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām sanatkumāro bhagavān idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Nārada said: In olden days, to the seers of disciplined souls who sought to know the truth, the blessed Sanatkumāra spoke these words.

sanskrit: nāsti vidyāsamaṃ cakṣur nāsti vidyāsamaṃ tapaḥ nāsti rāgasamaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti tyāgasamaṃ sukham
english: There is no eye like knowledge, there is no austerity like knowledge; there is no sorrow like passion, there is no happiness like renunciation.

sanskrit: nivṛttiḥ karmaṇaḥ pāpāt satataṃ puṇyaśīlatā sadvṛttiḥ samudācāraḥ śreya etad anuttamam
english: To turn away from sinful action, to be ever of meritorious disposition, good conduct and right behaviour — this is the unsurpassed good.

sanskrit: mānuṣyam asukhaṃ prāpya yaḥ sajjati sa muhyati nālaṃ sa duḥkhamokṣāya saṅgo vai duḥkhalakṣaṇam
english: He who, having attained this joyless human state, clings to it is deluded; he is unequal to release from sorrow, for attachment is the very mark of sorrow.

sanskrit: saktasya buddhiś calati mohajālavivardhinī mohajālāvṛto duḥkham iha cāmutra cāśnute
english: The mind of the man who clings wavers, swelling the net of delusion; wrapped in the net of delusion, he reaps sorrow both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: sarvopāyena kāmasya krodhasya ca vinigrahaḥ kāryaḥ śreyorthinā tau hi śreyoghātārtham udyatau
english: By every means the man who seeks the good must subdue desire and anger; for these two stand ready to destroy the good.

sanskrit: nityaṃ krodhāt tapo rakṣec chriyaṃ rakṣeta matsarāt vidyāṃ mānāvamānābhyām ātmānaṃ tu pramādataḥ
english: Let a man ever guard his austerity from anger, his prosperity from envy, his learning from honour and dishonour, and his own self from heedlessness.

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmaḥ kṣamā ca paramaṃ balam ātmajñānaṃ paraṃ jñānaṃ na satyād vidyate param
english: Freedom from cruelty is the highest dharma, and forbearance the highest strength; knowledge of the self is the highest knowledge, and nothing is found higher than truth.

sanskrit: satyasya vacanaṃ śreyaḥ satyād api hitaṃ bhavet yad bhūtahitam atyantam etat satyaṃ mataṃ mama
english: To speak the truth is good, yet even better than truth may be that which benefits; that which is of utmost benefit to living beings — this, in my view, is truth.

sanskrit: sarvārambhaphalatyāgī nirāśīr niṣparigrahaḥ yena sarvaṃ parityaktaṃ sa vidvān sa ca paṇḍitaḥ
english: He who renounces the fruit of all his undertakings, free of desire and free of possessions, he by whom all has been wholly let go — he is the wise, he is the learned man.

sanskrit: indriyair indriyārthebhyaś caraty ātmavaśair iha asajjamānaḥ śāntātmā nirvikāraḥ samāhitaḥ
english: With senses subject to the self he moves here among the objects of sense without cleaving to them, his soul at peace, unaltered, composed.

sanskrit: ātmabhūtair atadbhūtaḥ saha caiva vinaiva ca sa vimuktaḥ paraṃ śreyo nacireṇādhigacchati
english: Himself not bound to them, whether among those who are like himself or apart from them, he, being freed, before long attains the highest good.

sanskrit: adarśanam asaṃsparśas tathāsaṃbhāṣaṇaṃ sadā yasya bhūtaiḥ saha mune sa śreyo vindate param
english: He who, O sage, keeps ever without seeing, without touching, and without converse together with living beings — he finds the highest good.

sanskrit: na hiṃsyāt sarvabhūtāni maitrāyaṇagataś caret nedaṃ janma samāsādya vairaṃ kurvīta kena cit
english: Let him do no harm to any living being, and let him walk in the way of friendliness; having attained this birth, let him bear enmity toward none.

sanskrit: ākiṃcanyaṃ susaṃtoṣo nirāśīṣṭvam acāpalam etad āhuḥ paraṃ śreya ātmajñasya jitātmanaḥ
english: Possessing nothing, perfect contentment, freedom from craving, and steadiness — this, they say, is the highest good for the self-knower who has conquered himself.

sanskrit: parigrahaṃ parityajya bhava tāta jitendriyaḥ aśokaṃ sthānam ātiṣṭha iha cāmutra cābhayam
english: Renouncing possessions, become, my son, the conqueror of thy senses; take thy stand in the sorrowless state, free from fear both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: nirāmiṣā na śocanti tyajehāmiṣam ātmanaḥ parityajyāmiṣaṃ saumya duḥkhatāpād vimokṣyase
english: They who are without craving do not grieve; cast away the lure of the senses from thyself. Having renounced that lure, gentle one, thou shalt be freed from the burning of sorrow.

sanskrit: taponityena dāntena muninā saṃyatātmanā ajitaṃ jetukāmena bhāvyaṃ saṅgeṣv asaṅginā
english: The sage ever fixed in austerity, self-controlled, with disciplined soul, who longs to conquer the unconquered, must remain unattached amid all attachments.

sanskrit: guṇasaṅgeṣv anāsakta ekacaryārataḥ sadā brāhmaṇe nacirād eva sukham āyāty anuttamam
english: Unattached to the bonds of the qualities, ever delighting in the solitary life, the brāhmaṇa before long attains unsurpassed happiness.

sanskrit: dvaṃdvārāmeṣu bhūteṣu ya eko ramate muniḥ viddhi prajñānatṛptaṃ taṃ jñānatṛpto na śocati
english: Among beings that take their pleasure in pairs of opposites, the sage who delights alone — know him to be content in true wisdom; the one content in knowledge does not grieve.

sanskrit: śubhair labhati devatvaṃ vyāmiśrair janma mānuṣam aśubhaiś cāpy adhojanma karmabhir labhate 'vaśaḥ
english: By good deeds one wins godhood, by mixed deeds a human birth, and by evil deeds, helpless, one wins a lowly birth.

sanskrit: tatra mṛtyujarāduḥkhaiḥ satataṃ samabhidrutaḥ saṃsāre pacyate jantus tat kathaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: Therein, ceaselessly assailed by the sorrows of death and old age, the creature is cooked in the round of rebirth: how is it that thou dost not perceive this?

sanskrit: ahite hitasaṃjñas tvam adhruve dhruvasaṃjñakaḥ anarthe cārthasaṃjñas tvaṃ kimarthaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: In the harmful thou takest the harmful for the good, in the unstable for the stable, in the worthless for the worthwhile: why dost thou not awaken?

sanskrit: saṃveṣṭyamānaṃ bahubhir mohatantubhir ātmajaiḥ kośakāravad ātmānaṃ veṣṭayan nāvabudhyase
english: Wrapping thyself round, like a silkworm spinning its cocoon, with the many threads of delusion that are thine own offspring, thou dost not awaken.

sanskrit: alaṃ parigraheṇeha doṣavān hi parigrahaḥ kṛmir hi kośakāras tu badhyate svaparigrahāt
english: Enough of possessions here, for possession is a thing of fault; the silkworm, that little spinner, is bound by the very cocoon it makes its own.

sanskrit: putradārakuṭumbeṣu saktāḥ sīdanti jantavaḥ saraḥpaṅkārṇave magnā jīrṇā vanagajā iva
english: Clinging to sons, wives, and household, creatures sink down, foundering like aged forest elephants drowned in the mire of a pool.

sanskrit: mahājālasamākṛṣṭān sthale matsyān ivoddhṛtān snehajālasamākṛṣṭān paśya jantūn suduḥkhitān
english: Behold these creatures, sorely afflicted, dragged in by the net of affection, like fish drawn in by a great net and cast up upon dry land.

sanskrit: kuṭumbaṃ putradāraṃ ca śarīraṃ dravyasaṃcayāḥ pārakyam adhruvaṃ sarvaṃ kiṃ svaṃ sukṛtaduṣkṛtam
english: Household, sons and wife, the body, hoards of wealth — all belongs to others and is unstable; what is truly thine own save the good and ill that thou hast wrought?

sanskrit: yadā sarvaṃ parityajya gantavyam avaśena te anarthe kiṃ prasaktas tvaṃ svam arthaṃ nānutiṣṭhasi
english: When, abandoning all, thou must depart helpless, why art thou bent upon the worthless and dost not pursue thine own true good?

sanskrit: aviśrāntam anālambam apātheyam adaiśikam tamaḥkāntāram adhvānaṃ katham eko gamiṣyasi
english: How wilt thou travel alone that road which is the wilderness of darkness — without rest, without support, without provisions, without a guide?

sanskrit: na hi tvā prasthitaṃ kaś cit pṛṣṭhato 'nugamiṣyati sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ ca tvā yāsyantam anuyāsyati
english: For when thou hast set forth, none will follow at thy back; only thy good and ill deeds will go after thee as thou departest.

sanskrit: vidyā karma ca śauryaṃ ca jñānaṃ ca bahuvistaram arthārtham anusāryante siddhārthas tu vimucyate
english: Learning, action, valour, and far-reaching knowledge are pursued for the sake of gain; but he whose end is achieved is set free.

sanskrit: nibandhanī rajjur eṣā yā grāme vasato ratiḥ chittvaināṃ sukṛto yānti naināṃ chindanti duṣkṛtaḥ
english: That delight of one who dwells in the village is the binding rope; cutting it, the doers of good go free, but the doers of evil cut it not.

sanskrit: rūpakūlāṃ manaḥsrotāṃ sparśadvīpāṃ rasāvahām gandhapaṅkāṃ śabdajalāṃ svargamārgadurāvahām
english: Whose banks are forms, whose current is the mind, whose island is touch, that bears along taste; whose mud is smell, whose water is sound, hard to ferry on the road to heaven —

sanskrit: kṣamāritrāṃ satyamayīṃ dharmasthairyavaṭākarām tyāgavātādhvagāṃ śīghrāṃ buddhināvā nadīṃ taret
english: that swift river, whose oar is forbearance, whose substance is truth, whose harbour-banyan is steadfastness in dharma, traversed by the wind of renunciation — let him cross it by the boat of the understanding.

sanskrit: tyaja dharmam adharmaṃ ca ubhe satyānṛte tyaja ubhe satyānṛte tyaktvā yena tyajasi taṃ tyaja
english: Renounce dharma and unrighteousness, renounce both truth and falsehood; and having renounced both truth and falsehood, renounce that by which thou renouncest.

sanskrit: tyaja dharmam asaṃkalpād adharmaṃ cāpy ahiṃsayā ubhe satyānṛte buddhyā buddhiṃ paramaniścayāt
english: Renounce dharma by ceasing to will, and unrighteousness by non-harming; renounce both truth and falsehood by the understanding, and the understanding itself by the highest resolve.

sanskrit: asthisthūṇaṃ snāyuyutaṃ māṃsaśoṇitalepanam carmāvanaddhaṃ durgandhi pūrṇaṃ mūtrapurīṣayoḥ
english: Its pillars are bones, knit together by sinews, plastered over with flesh and blood, bound round with skin, foul-smelling, filled with urine and dung —

sanskrit: jarāśokasamāviṣṭaṃ rogāyatanam āturam rajasvalam anityaṃ ca bhūtāvāsaṃ samutsṛja
english: beset by age and grief, the abode of disease, ailing, defiled with passion and impermanent — cast off this dwelling-place of the elements.

sanskrit: idaṃ viśvaṃ jagat sarvam ajagac cāpi yad bhavet mahābhūtātmakaṃ sarvaṃ mahad yat paramāṇu yat
english: This whole moving universe and whatever is unmoving — all that is great and all that is the minutest atom — is in essence composed of the great elements.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi ca pañcaiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajas tathā ity eṣa saptadaśako rāśir avyaktasaṃjñakaḥ
english: The five senses, and tamas, sattva, and rajas — thus this aggregate of seventeen is named the Unmanifest.

sanskrit: sarvair ihendriyārthaiś ca vyaktāvyaktair hi saṃhitaḥ pañcaviṃśaka ity eṣa vyaktāvyaktamayo guṇaḥ
english: Joined here with all the objects of sense, both manifest and unmanifest, this becomes the group of twenty-five, the principle made up of the manifest and the unmanifest.

sanskrit: etaiḥ sarvaiḥ samāyuktaḥ pumān ity abhidhīyate trivargo 'tra sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ tathā
english: United with all these, it is called the Person; herein lie the triad of aims, pleasure and pain, life and likewise death.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ veda tattvena sa veda prabhavāpyayau pārāśaryeha boddhavyaṃ jñānānāṃ yac ca kiṃ cana
english: He who knows this in truth knows the origin and the dissolution of things; here, O son of Parāśara's line, is what is to be understood, and whatever else there is of all the kinds of knowledge.

sanskrit: indriyair gṛhyate yad yat tat tad vyaktam iti sthitiḥ avyaktam iti vijñeyaṃ liṅgagrāhyam atīndriyam
english: Whatever is grasped by the senses, that stands as the manifest; what lies beyond the senses, apprehended only by its marks, is to be known as the unmanifest.

sanskrit: indriyair niyatair dehī dhārābhir iva tarpyate loke vitatam ātmānaṃ lokaṃ cātmani paśyati
english: The embodied one is nourished by the restrained senses, as if by streams of water; he beholds the self spread through the world, and the world within the self.

sanskrit: parāvaradṛśaḥ śaktir jñānavelāṃ na paśyati paśyataḥ sarvabhūtāni sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā
english: The power of one who sees the higher and the lower beholds no shore of knowledge, even as he sees all beings in every condition and at all times.

sanskrit: brahmabhūtasya saṃyogo nāśubhenopapadyate jñānena vividhān kleśān ativṛttasya mohajān loke buddhiprakāśena lokamārgo na riṣyate
english: For one who has become the Absolute no contact with evil arises; for him who by knowledge has transcended the manifold afflictions born of delusion, the path of the world is not lost in the light of his understanding.

sanskrit: anādinidhanaṃ jantum ātmani sthitam avyayam akartāram amūrtaṃ ca bhagavān āha tīrthavit
english: The creature without beginning or end, abiding in the self, imperishable, the non-doer and the formless — so the blessed knower of the sacred fords has declared.

sanskrit: yo jantuḥ svakṛtais tais taiḥ karmabhir nityaduḥkhitaḥ sa duḥkhapratighātārthaṃ hanti jantūn anekadhā
english: The creature ever made wretched by those very deeds he himself has done, in order to ward off his own pain, slays other creatures in manifold ways.

sanskrit: tataḥ karma samādatte punar anyan navaṃ bahu tapyate 'tha punas tena bhuktvāpathyam ivāturaḥ
english: Thereupon he takes on yet again much fresh deeds, and again is tormented by them, like a sick man who has eaten what is harmful to him.

sanskrit: ajasram eva mohārto duḥkheṣu sukhasaṃjñitaḥ badhyate mathyate caiva karmabhir manthavat sadā
english: Stricken with delusion without cease, taking his sorrows for happiness, he is bound and churned forever by his deeds, as butter is churned by the churning-stick.

sanskrit: tato nivṛtto bandhāt svāt karmaṇām udayād iha paribhramati saṃsāraṃ cakravad bahuvedanaḥ
english: Then, even when freed from one bond of his own, through the rising up of fresh deeds here below, he wanders round the round of rebirth like a wheel, suffering many pains.
